annotations.text:
Pay is read-only and computed live from the time records — the same way /pay/stats already works, so it never waits for anyone to press Build.

Because the figures can still move, the screen says how far along the week is: recorded, in review, approved, paid. Export sits in the corner and hands you whatever the period row is showing.

The week blocks you asked about: week number, dates, job count, hours, money and where the week stands — grouped under a month header carrying the month's own total. A week belongs to the month its Monday falls in, so these figures match the existing monthly export.

Payroll opens on a WEEK, not a person — the manager's real question is "who do I owe this week". One Build covers everybody, and somebody with no rate is called out in red rather than passing as an ordinary $0.00 line.

Tapping a row opens that person's week, where approving is the first thing on screen rather than below three cards.

Direct Supervisor now lists only people who can approve payroll: managers and administrators.

The warning block is the migration case — people whose current supervisor no longer qualifies. Worth deciding whether we move them automatically or make you do it.

The same screen as the open week, in the state it ends up in. Arriving from the week list or from a month lands on this one page either way — the day breakdown is a section of it, not a screen of its own.

Only the tracker, the sentence under it and the money have moved on.
